summary: Original representative lung acinus: terminal conducting airway, respiratory bronchioles, alveolar duct/sac spaces, septa and separate pulmonary inflow/capillary/outflow routes. Five rings summarize bronchiolar muscle. Air is a void and blood lumens are implicit; the corner cut is an educational removal. Gas exchange is taught by relationship and text because this original has no separate barrier layers. Review v2 is a separate model.

descriptions.Terminal bronchiole: Terminal bronchiole: conducting airway before the gas-exchanging region. Its open lumen, wall and representative wall-seated club cells are retained. Ciliated and club-cell biology is explained; no ciliary motion is modeled. DRAFT AWAITING USER REVIEW. Mixed-scale teaching geometry; no patient morphometry.
descriptions.Respiratory bronchioles: Respiratory bronchioles: transitional airways with alveolar openings. These two representative branches lead into duct and sac regions; the reduced hierarchy is not an entire human acinus. DRAFT AWAITING USER REVIEW. Mixed-scale teaching geometry; no patient morphometry.
descriptions.Bronchiolar smooth muscle: Bronchiolar smooth muscle: five retained rings on the terminal bronchiole illustrate circumferential muscle location. Real bronchiolar muscle has an oblique/spiral arrangement; these rings do not reconstruct that fiber course or generate contraction. DRAFT AWAITING USER REVIEW. Mixed-scale teaching geometry; no patient morphometry.
descriptions.Pulmonary arteriole (deoxygenated): Pulmonary arteriole: arterial inflow from the right heart carries relatively deoxygenated blood toward the alveolar capillary bed. Blue encodes oxygenation, while artery identifies direction in the circulation. This is a representative hollow wall and source-authored inlet route. DRAFT AWAITING USER REVIEW. Mixed-scale teaching geometry; no patient morphometry.
descriptions.Pulmonary venule (oxygenated): Pulmonary venule: venous outflow carries oxygenated blood from the capillary bed toward the left heart. Red is an oxygenation cue, not the definition of an artery. Peripheral drainage is represented schematically. DRAFT AWAITING USER REVIEW. Mixed-scale teaching geometry; no patient morphometry.
descriptions.Alveolar capillaries: Alveolar capillaries: hollow interconnected teaching loops in fitted septal channels. Blue-to-red vertex color uses an unchanged spatial field; it is not measured oxygen saturation, velocity, transit time or a perfusion solution. Endothelium is implicit in the wall. DRAFT AWAITING USER REVIEW. Mixed-scale teaching geometry; no patient morphometry.
descriptions.Interalveolar septa – respiratory bronch: Respiratory-region alveolar septal tissue: this exact selectable source part is an x-slab of a shared tissue matrix. It outlines nearby airspaces; its slab boundary is a teaching partition, not an anatomical membrane. DRAFT AWAITING USER REVIEW. Mixed-scale teaching geometry; no patient morphometry.
descriptions.Interalveolar septa – alveolar ducts: Duct-region alveolar septal tissue: thin tissue around represented alveolar openings with fitted capillary channels. This exact selectable part is the middle x-slab of a shared matrix. Type I lining, basement membrane and endothelium are not separate selectable layers here. DRAFT AWAITING USER REVIEW. Mixed-scale teaching geometry; no patient morphometry.
descriptions.Interalveolar septa – alveolar sacs: Sac-region alveolar septal tissue: distal tissue around representative sac spaces. Its x-slab grouping does not establish an anatomical capsule. Fourteen total alveolar spaces summarize a much larger branching acinus. DRAFT AWAITING USER REVIEW. Mixed-scale teaching geometry; no patient morphometry.
descriptions.Pores of Kohn: Pores of Kohn: three retained annular tissue rims surrounding bores between paired airspaces. The selected mesh is septal tissue, while the central hole is air. Saved connectivity and both neighboring hosts must be checked before claiming actual pore communication. DRAFT AWAITING USER REVIEW. Mixed-scale teaching geometry; no patient morphometry.
descriptions.Type II pneumocytes: Type II pneumocytes: two representative cells per alveolus, locally normal-aligned and seated in fitted tissue recesses. They secrete surfactant and contribute to epithelial repair. Surfactant film, secretion kinetics and repair motion are explained in text, not built as additional structures. DRAFT AWAITING USER REVIEW. Mixed-scale teaching geometry; no patient morphometry.
descriptions.Alveolar macrophages: Alveolar macrophages: four retained spherical luminal exemplars in assigned airspaces. They illustrate phagocytosis and surfactant clearance. Cell shape, migration, lymphatic exit and mucociliary routes are not reconstructed or animated. DRAFT AWAITING USER REVIEW. Mixed-scale teaching geometry; no patient morphometry.
descriptions.Club (Clara) cells: Club (Clara) cells: ten retained secretory cell exemplars fitted to the bowed terminal airway wall and projecting into its lumen. Club-cell secretion and context-dependent metabolism/repair are explained; cell counts, cilia and toxin-response kinetics are schematic. DRAFT AWAITING USER REVIEW. Mixed-scale teaching geometry; no patient morphometry.
descriptions.Alveolar duct smooth muscle (knobs): Alveolar duct smooth muscle (knobs): retained discrete knobs illustrate muscle at duct-mouth rims. They are solid tissue, not vessel walls or moving pumps. Exact rim seating requires saved-output and native-view checks. DRAFT AWAITING USER REVIEW. Mixed-scale teaching geometry; no patient morphometry.
